comments.text: It's famously said that Lake Superior never gives up her dead. When investigating some shipwrecks, they would find bodies in surprisingly preserved condition, clothing included. It's kind of hauntingly beautiful. When bodies normally decay via putrefaction, bacteria break things down and produce gases, causing bodies to bloat and float. However, the bottom of the lake is so cold and low in oxygen that this process doesn't happen, and instead the fats undergo saponification! This happens via anaerobic bacterial hydrolysis, and creates what's known as "corpse wax" or adipocere. Obviously, Lake Superior doesn't have an exclusive claim on this process as it happens anywhere it's cold enough and anaerobic enough. It's also one of the mechanisms that result in "bog bodies." It should be noted that peat bogs are often acidic as well and have some additional factors that basically pickle bodies, preserving soft tissues and dissolving hard ones like bone.
